chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hudhayn ibn Mukhariq, Abu Junada al-Salouli, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: 'Whoever fasts (the month of) Sha'ban will have a purification from every unintentional mistake, disgrace, and gesture.' Abu Hamza said: Then I said to Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him: 'What is the disgrace?' He said: 'The oath (made with the right hand) in an act of disobedience; and there is no vow in an act of disobedience.' I said: 'Then what is the gesture?' He said: 'The oath during anger; and the repentance from it is to regret upon it.'

key_terms.بَادِرَة: Badirah (a gesture or impulsive act, specifically linked to oaths in anger)
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.وَصْمَة: Wasmah (disgrace or stigma, specifically linked to oaths in disobedience)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of fasting in Sha'ban and what do 'wasmah' and 'badirah' mean in this context?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration linking the voluntary fasting of Sha'ban to spiritual purification from three specific categories of minor sins: unintentional slips (*zallah*), disgraceful oaths in disobedience (*wasmah*), and impulsive oaths born of anger (*badirah*). This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on Sha'ban as a preparatory month for Ramadan, where fasting serves not only as worship but as a mechanism for cleansing the soul of the lingering effects of rash speech and vows. The detailed definitions provided by Imam al-Sadiq highlight the importance of mindfulness in one's vows and emotional state during acts of devotion.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, from his paternal uncle, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Kufi, from Hudhayn ibn Mukhariq, Abu Junada al-Salouli, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja’far, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The one who fasts (the month of) Sha’ban will have a purification from every unintentional mistake, disgrace and gesture. Abu Hamza said: Then I said to Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him: What is the disgrace? He said: The right hand (in promise) in an act of disobedience; there is no oath (valid) in an act of disobedience. I said: Then what is the gesture? He said: The right hand (in promise) during anger; the repentance from it is to regret upon it.
